# Draft — PR numbers and durations for the 11 curated levadas

**Drafted 2026-08-17 for veto (D-064's method).** One line per levada, what I think it is,
and where the figure came from. **Flagged rows are the ones I think are wrong.**

**Generated by** `node tools/levada-routes.mjs`, which asks OSM for the signed walking-route
relations near each levada's trailheads. Nothing here was typed from memory, and nothing was
written into `content/` — that waits for your veto.

## Where the times come from, and why they are not measurements

⚠ **One walk sets the pace for all of them.** You walked PR18 there-and-back in *"+3 hours"*.
OSM gives PR18 as 5.3 km signed, so ~10.6 km round, so **~3.4 km/h including stops.** Every
other time in the table is that pace applied to that levada's distance.

The tool reproduces PR18 as **3h07** against your "+3 hours", which is the only check available
and is circular — it is the walk the pace came from. Treat the other ten as arithmetic.

⚠ **They are floors, not estimates, and the reason is yours:** narrow sections force you to
**wait for people to cross**, so a popular levada in peak hours is slower than this. PR18 was
*"kind of empty because it was at the end of the day"* — the fast case, used as the baseline for
everything. Expect the real numbers to come in above these.

## The findings, in the order they matter

### F1 — Levada do Furado: the signed distance is longer than the mapped course
PR 10 is signed 11 km; OSM has mapped 7.6 km of channel. Either the signed route continues past
what is mapped, or PR 10 covers more than this levada (it is often walked as Ribeiro Frio →
Portela, which is more than the Furado). **The 22 km / 6h30 is probably too long for what a user
would call "doing the Levada do Furado".**

### F2 — Five levadas have no signed route at all, and enormous mapped courses
`LNS`, `LNCalheta`, `LRJ`, `LC`, `LF` are levada abbreviations, not PR numbers — I counted them
as PR routes on the first run, which was wrong, and the tool now refuses to.

These are **irrigation channels, not signed walks**, and their mapped courses run to **40.2 km
(Norte)** and **28.9 km (Nova da Calheta)**. This is exactly what `docs/field-notes.md` warned
about: *"the drawn course is however much of the channel OSM happens to have mapped."* No
there-and-back figure is offered for them, because nobody walks 80 km.

⚠ **This has a live consequence for D-065.** The fraction rule is `covered ≥ 60% of course`. On a
there-and-back you cover the channel once, so a 3-hour walk on Levada do Norte covers ~5 km of a
40 km course — **13%.** The fraction rule is **unreachable** on these five, and the stamp rests
entirely on the 3 km absolute (`WALKED_ABSOLUTE_M`) and the 45-minute rule (D-068). Both fire, so
nothing is broken — but half the pack is credited by a path the fraction rule was written to be
the primary of, and that should be known rather than discovered.

### F3 — Levada do Caldeirão Verde is matched to the wrong route
The tool picked **PR 9.1 at 1.9 km**. PR 9.1 is the *Caldeirão do Inferno* extension, not the
Caldeirão Verde walk, and 1.9 km is far too short — the mapped course is 7.1 km. **I believe the
right answer is PR 9, and I have not verified it.** This is the row I am least confident in and
the one most worth your eye, because Caldeirão Verde is one of the island's best-known walks.

### F4 — PR 28 for Levada da Rocha Vermelha looks doubtful
The official PR network is numbered into the low twenties as far as I know, so **PR 28 may be a
mapper's invention or a route I do not know about.** The distance (10.8 km) is plausible. Do not
let this into `content/` on my word.

## My recommendation, which is not what you asked for

**Do not use these durations to set the crediting threshold. Put them on the place card instead.**

Two reasons:

1. **A per-levada threshold would make the hard levadas harder.** Scaling the 45 minutes to each
   levada's length means the long, remote, canopy-heavy ones demand the most — and those are
   precisely where GPS drops fixes and where under-crediting is most likely. A flat generous
   floor is the shape D-009 and your own instruction ask for. Against these figures, **45 minutes
   is 12–30% of a real walk** — very generous, deliberately, exactly as you said you wanted.
2. **The durations are worth much more as content than as logic.** *"Levada do Rei · PR 18 ·
   5.3 km · about 3 hours there and back"* is the single most useful line you could add to a
   place card for somebody deciding what to do today. The card already exists (D-052), and this
   is the kind of Madeira knowledge that belongs in `content/` (D-017).

So: **keep `WALKED_MINUTES = 45`. Ship the numbers as content.** If you agree, the work is a
`prRef`, `signedKm` and `typicalDuration` field on the levada entries — but the values must clear
F1–F4 first, and F3 is wrong today.

## What I need from you

1. **F3** — is Caldeirão Verde PR 9? (I am fairly sure, but not sure enough to write it.)
2. **F4** — does PR 28 exist?
3. **F1** — is "Levada do Furado" the Ribeiro Frio → Portela walk, or the shorter piece?
4. Whether the five unsigned levadas (F2) should carry a duration **at all**. They are channels
   people walk part of, so a single number may be the wrong shape for them.
